name: Polvo
label: Merge
lede: Ash Bowie and Dave Brylawski met in a Spanish class at UNC and named their band after the Spanish word for dust. Bowie broke strings and kept playing, and Polvo's records got stranger from there, though Bowie says it was never as complicated as people think.

eras.title: A Spanish class at UNC
eras.text: Ash Bowie and Dave Brylawski met in a Spanish class at the University of North Carolina, bonding over SST records and Mitch Easter's Let's Active. With bassist Steve Popson and a jazz-minded drummer, Eddie Watkins, they gave themselves the Spanish word for dust.

years.h: Two UNC classmates start Polvo with a jazz-minded drummer
years.p: Ash Bowie and Dave Brylawski form the band in Chapel Hill with drummer Eddie Watkins. Bassist Steve Popson joins soon after.
years.xp:
Popson called Watkins the most experienced player of the four. He brought jazz ideas and unusual drumming that set the band's template, and at first the four felt like outsiders in the Chapel Hill scene.

Bowie says he found his guitar sound by accident: he broke strings and, instead of restringing, played on with about four and wandered the tuning.

years.h: Can I Ride is the first Polvo record, on Kitchen Puff
years.p: Kitchen Puff Records puts out a seven-song double 7-inch. Can I Ride and Vibracobra get re-recorded for the first album.
years.xp: A version of Can I Ride turns up in Half-Cocked, the 1995 indie-rock road movie. The double single was later reissued as the Polvo EP.

eras.title: Slack strings, Merge and a road movie
eras.text: Polvo signed to Merge Records, the label Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance of Superchunk ran out of Chapel Hill. Bowie's guitars sounded like they were melting, and critics reached for Sonic Youth and Gentle Giant in the same review.

years.h: Four days in Raleigh, mostly live to tape
years.p: Polvo record Cor-Crane Secret at Jerry Kee's Duck Kee Studios from January 2 to 5, 1992. Merge releases it that year.
years.xp: Bowie's sound came partly from breaking strings and playing on in slack tunings, with a push from My Bloody Valentine's Isn't Anything. A Casio MT-65, the keyboard that can play every sound on the Ghostbusters theme, shows up on every Polvo record; Bowie has had it since he was 13.

years.h: A cover Jehovah's Witnesses didn't want on a record
years.p: Produced by [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]] in four December days, Today's Active Lifestyles comes out on Merge. The original cover art is pulled after a copyright dispute with the Jehovah's Witnesses.
years.xp:
Early pressings showed red tigers on a yellow background. The Talkhouse interview says the original art drew on old circus posters. When Merge reissued the record in 2020, the cover kept only the tigers, and the band maintained the original design came from public-domain sources.

The album leaned hard into the Middle Eastern modes that would define Polvo. Hot Press compared it to Sonic Youth with untuned guitars.

years.h: Celebrate the New Dark Age lands between albums
years.p: The EP is Polvo's Merge release between the second album and the move to Touch and Go. The band also turns up that year in Half-Cocked.

years.cap: Polvo outside a corner shop, c. 1994
years.h: Bowie follows Mary Timony to Boston
years.p: Ash Bowie moves to be with his girlfriend [[Mary Timony|d9c8dc3c-15b8-40d5-8153-ae9214aeef55]] of [[Helium|573510d6-bb5d-4d07-b0aa-ea6afe39e28d]] and plays bass in her band. Polvo is now split across two cities.
Polvo's EP is the last release of their first run on Merge. The next records go to Chicago's Touch and Go.

eras.title: A double album, then everybody scatters
eras.text: Polvo moved to Touch and Go and went big with a double album. Then life pulled the band apart: the drummer had a family, one guitarist was in Boston, the other headed for New York and India.

years.h: Touch and Go gets a double album
years.p: Exploded Drawing, Polvo's first record for the Chicago label, is its longest and most ambitious, with Indian and Middle Eastern drones stretched over two discs.

years.big: He was the first person in the band to have kids
years.h: Eddie Watkins leaves after three albums
years.p: Drummer Eddie Watkins quits Polvo after three albums, three EPs and five singles. Steve Popson says it wasn't totally unexpected: Watkins had gotten married.

years.h: Shapes is the last album before the split
years.p: Brian Walsby takes over the drums for the Touch and Go record. Dave Brylawski is headed to graduate school in New York and trips to India.

years.h: Two nights at the Cat's Cradle end it
years.p: Polvo finish a farewell US tour with a two-night stand at their hometown club in Carrboro and split amicably.

eras.title: Libraness, Idyll Swords and a bar in Raleigh
eras.text: Nobody quit music. Bowie made records under a new name, Brylawski played Indonesian-inflected music, and Popson ran a club.

years.p: Ash Bowie releases Yesterday...and Tomorrow's Shells on Tiger Style Records.

years.h: Brylawski plays Indonesian-flavored trio music; Popson opens a bar
years.p: Dave Brylawski joins the Indonesian-influenced trio Idyll Swords and later teams with Steve Popson in [[Black Taj|0e01b620-8cd8-4637-9480-1ebbae6a82ef]]. Popson owns Kings, a Raleigh music club.

eras.title: All Tomorrow's Parties calls
eras.text: A festival invitation got the three original songwriters back in a room after a decade. With a new drummer they rewrote the old songs instead of replaying them, then made two more albums for Merge.

years.h: All Tomorrow's Parties calls, and Polvo picks up
years.p: Invited to play the festival and Barcelona's Primavera Sound, Polvo re-form with Brian Quast, formerly of [[The Cherry Valence|3298a4be-175c-43ac-b749-6107b0222112]], on drums.
years.xp: The band didn't replay the '90s records note for note. Bowie told Talkhouse he wanted to write new lyrics and change some parts around, so the reunion sets reworked older songs.

years.p: Back on Merge, Polvo release their first studio album since 1997, timed to the label's 20th anniversary.

years.h: Siberia comes out and nobody is told
years.p: Polvo's sixth album arrives on Merge with no promotion behind it. The band's last live show, per Wikipedia, was in 2011.

eras.title: Losing Eddie, finding the old records
eras.text: The original drummer died young. A few years later Merge reissued the first two albums, and the band admitted they liked them more than they'd remembered.

years.h: Eddie Watkins, Polvo's first drummer, dies at 47
years.p: Watkins dies on a Sunday evening in Durham. No cause of death was made public.
years.xp: After Polvo he worked as a senior project manager at LexisNexis and played drums in Stranger in the Valley of the Kings. Superchunk drummer Jon Wurster remembered his economy of movement, and said Jim dubbed him "The Chef."

years.big: I can hear Steve's parts better on the remaster
years.h: Merge reissues the first two albums
years.p: Ash Bowie, who hadn't listened to the old records in about 20 years, says he finally had "a Polvo day," and the line above is his.
